test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Data Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records data at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all designated GMP storage areas.
System access credentials are available.

test_steps.action: Log in to the EMS software using valid credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully logged into the EMS application.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the real-time monitoring screen for a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: Real-time temperature readings for the selected storage area are displayed.

test_steps.action: Observe the temperature readings for a period of at least 10 minutes, noting the timestamps of each recorded reading.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are continuously updated, and the time difference between consecutive readings does not exceed 5 minutes.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of each recorded temperature reading

test_steps.action: Access the historical data log for the observed period and verify the recorded timestamps and temperature values.
test_steps.expected_result: Historical data accurately reflects the observed real-time readings, with timestamps confirming the recording interval is 5 minutes or less.
data_to_capture: Historical data log entries (timestamp and temperature)

acceptance_criteria: The EMS continuously displays real-time temperature readings.
All recorded temperature data points have timestamps that are no more than 5 minutes apart.
Historical data accurately reflects the observed real-time monitoring.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be accurate and complete.
Timestamps must be precise and reliable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range, Accuracy, and Alarm Generation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates within the specified temperature range, maintains the required accuracy, and generates alerts when temperature deviates from the setpoint.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all designated GMP storage areas.
A calibrated reference thermometer is available for comparison.
System access credentials are available.
Setpoint and alarm deviation values are configured in the system.

test_steps.action: Log in to the EMS software using valid credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully logged into the EMS application.

test_steps.action: Place the calibrated reference thermometer adjacent to a temperature sensor in a GMP storage area and record the EMS reading and reference thermometer reading.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS temperature reading is within ±0.5°C of the reference thermometer reading.

test_steps.action: Adjust the temperature in the storage area (using controlled means, e.g., environmental chamber or by adjusting HVAC) to simulate a deviation from the setpoint, ensuring the temperature remains within the -80°C to +50°C range.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS continues to display temperature readings within the specified range.

test_steps.action: Continue adjusting the temperature to trigger a deviation of ±2°C from the configured setpoint for the storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is generated by the EMS within 30 seconds of the temperature deviating ±2°C from the setpoint.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm is logged in the system's audit trail with appropriate details.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm event is recorded in the audit trail, including the time, type of alarm, user who acknowledged it (if applicable), and the temperature at the time of the alarm.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry for the alarm

acceptance_criteria: Temperature readings from the EMS are accurate within ±0.5°C compared to a calibrated reference thermometer.
The EMS operates and records data within the specified temperature range of -80°C to +50°C.
Alarms are generated within 30 seconds when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
All alarm events are accurately logged in the system's audit trail.
data_integrity_requirements: Temperature readings must be accurate and within specified tolerance.
Alarm events must be reliably detected and logged.
Audit trail must capture all critical events.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Unmodified and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor-supplied software is used without modification and that all data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and operational.
Access to system logs and configuration files is available.
Documentation of vendor-supplied software version is available.

test_steps.action: Review system installation and configuration documentation to confirm no modifications were made to the vendor-supplied software.
test_steps.expected_result: Documentation confirms that the vendor-supplied software has not been modified.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS database and examine the format of stored temperature and humidity data.
test_steps.expected_result: The stored data is in the vendor's standard database format as specified in the vendor documentation.

acceptance_criteria: The system configuration and installation records confirm that the vendor-supplied software was installed as-is without any modifications.
The format of the stored environmental monitoring data matches the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored in a format that ensures its integrity and is retrievable.
Unmodified software reduces the risk of introducing unintended data handling issues.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains an audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11 and utilizes vendor's built-in electronic signature functionality.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and operational.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
Access to system audit logs and electronic signature features is available.

test_steps.action: Perform a user login and a configuration change (e.g., adjust a setpoint) and verify that an entry is created in the audit trail.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail logs the user login, the action performed (configuration change), the date, time, and the user who performed the action.

test_steps.action: Initiate a process that requires an electronic signature (e.g., approving a report or acknowledging an alarm) and verify the electronic signature is captured.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for and captures a valid electronic signature, including user ID, date, time, and reason for signature, using the vendor's built-in functionality.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail to ensure it meets the requirements of 21 CFR Part 11, including immutability and traceability.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail is complete, accurate, and cannot be altered or deleted without a record of the alteration.

acceptance_criteria: The system's audit trail accurately records all significant events, including user actions, date, time, and the user responsible.
Electronic signatures are captured using the vendor's standard functionality and meet the requirements of 21 CFR Part 11.
The audit trail is immutable and traceable.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trails must be secure, time-stamped, and retained.
Electronic signatures must be unique, attributable, and legally binding.
Ensures data integrity and regulatory compliance for electronic records.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Usage for Batch Release and Data Archival
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system utilizes vendor-provided standard reports for batch release and that data archival functions correctly for the required retention period.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to test archival.
Access to vendor-provided standard reports is available.

test_steps.action: Generate a standard report for a specific batch using the vendor's built-in reporting functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: The generated report accurately reflects the environmental monitoring data for the specified batch and is in the vendor's standard format.

test_steps.action: Initiate the data archival process for data older than the defined retention period (e.g., 7 years).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully archives the specified historical data, making it inaccessible for routine use but retrievable via the archival feature.
data_to_capture: Verification of data removal from active storage (if applicable)

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve archived data from the vendor's archival feature.
test_steps.expected_result: The archived data is successfully retrieved and is consistent with the data that was archived.

acceptance_criteria: Standard reports are generated correctly and used for batch release as per URS-EMS-007.
Data archival process successfully moves data to the archive as per URS-EMS-010.
Archived data is retrievable and consistent.
data_integrity_requirements: Data in reports must be accurate and complete.
Archived data must be preserved and retrievable without corruption.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Alarm Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system meets the required availability percentage and that alarm notifications are correctly integrated with the site paging system.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Site paging system is operational and configured for integration.
Access to system logs and monitoring tools is available.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a defined period (e.g., 7 days) excluding planned maintenance windows.
test_steps.expected_result: The system uptime is at least 99.5% of the monitored period.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alarm within 30 seconds of the deviation.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is successfully sent to the site paging system via the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: The site paging system receives the alarm notification, and the notification content is accurate.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of notification receipt by paging system

acceptance_criteria: System availability is 99.5% or higher, excluding planned maintenance, as per URS-EMS-013.
Alarm response time is within 30 seconds as per URS-EMS-011.
Alarm notifications are successfully integrated with the site paging system as per URS-EMS-015.
data_integrity_requirements: System availability ensures continuous monitoring.
Accurate and timely alarm notifications are critical for product safety.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage Capacity and System Response Time for Alarms
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can store data for at least 10 years and that alarm conditions are responded to within 30 seconds.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and configured.
Access to system logs and performance monitoring tools.
Knowledge of system architecture and database.

test_steps.action: Simulate continuous data generation for a period equivalent to 10 years of expected usage, or utilize system tools to project storage needs based on current rates.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's data storage capacity is sufficient to accommodate 10 years of continuous monitoring data without performance degradation or data loss.

test_steps.action: Induce a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition (e.g., exceed the upper or lower alarm threshold).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates an alarm notification and logs the event within 30 seconds of the deviation occurring.
data_to_capture: System logs detailing alarm event and response time.

acceptance_criteria: System storage capacity meets or exceeds the requirement for 10 years of data.
Alarm response time is consistently within the 30-second limit.
data_integrity_requirements: Data storage must be reliable and prevent data loss over the 10-year period.
Timely alarm notification is critical for product protection.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Integration with Site Paging System and Facility Management System
test_cases.objective: To confirm that the EMS system successfully integrates with the site paging system for alarm notifications and the facility management system for data exchange.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and configured.
Site paging system is operational and accessible.
Facility management system is operational and accessible.
Vendor API documentation for paging system integration.
Documentation for facility management system interface protocols.

test_steps.action: Trigger an alarm condition in the EMS system that is configured to send notifications to the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is successfully sent to the site paging system via the vendor API, and the designated personnel receive the alert.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of alarm trigger in EMS.
Record of notification sent via vendor API.
Confirmation of receipt of alert by designated personnel.

test_steps.action: Verify data exchange between the EMS system and the facility management system using standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: Relevant environmental data (e.g., temperature, humidity) is accurately transferred from the EMS to the facility management system as per the defined interface.
data_to_capture: Corresponding data points in facility management system.
Verification of data accuracy and completeness.

acceptance_criteria: Alarm notifications are reliably transmitted to the site paging system.
Data exchange with the facility management system is accurate and complete.
data_integrity_requirements: Timely and accurate alarm notifications are crucial for product safety.
Consistent and correct data transfer to the facility management system is important for overall facility oversight.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Retention and Archival Feature
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly retains data for 7 years and utilizes the vendor's archival feature as per URS-EMS-010.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to simulate a 7-year retention period.
Access to system administration and archival functions.

test_steps.action: Simulate or identify data that is older than 7 years based on the system's current operational date.
test_steps.expected_result: The system should identify data older than 7 years.
data_to_capture: Identification of data older than 7 years

test_steps.action: Initiate the vendor's archival feature for the identified historical data.
test_steps.expected_result: The archival process completes successfully without errors.

test_steps.action: Verify that the archived data is no longer accessible through the standard reporting interface but can be retrieved using the archival retrieval function.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data is not visible in standard reports, but is retrievable via the archival mechanism.

acceptance_criteria: Data older than 7 years is successfully archived.
Archived data is inaccessible via standard reporting.
Archived data is retrievable using the designated archival retrieval function.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-010: Data shall be retained for 7 years using vendor's archival feature.
data_integrity_requirements: Data retention period is met.
Data is not lost during archival.
Archived data remains intact and retrievable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Planned Maintenance Exclusion
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system meets the 99.5% availability requirement, excluding periods of planned maintenance, as per URS-EMS-013.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is operational.
System logs are accessible for review.
Schedule of planned maintenance activities is available.

test_steps.action: Collect system uptime and downtime logs for a defined period (e.g., 30 days).
test_steps.expected_result: System logs accurately record all operational and downtime events.

test_steps.action: Identify and exclude any downtime periods that correspond to documented planned maintenance activities.
test_steps.expected_result: Planned maintenance downtime is clearly identified and segregated from unplanned downtime.
data_to_capture: List of planned maintenance dates and durations

test_steps.action: Calculate the system availability percentage based on the total operational time versus the total time in the defined period, excluding planned maintenance.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated availability percentage is 99.5% or higher.

acceptance_criteria: System availability is calculated to be 99.5% or greater.
Downtime attributed to planned maintenance is correctly excluded from the availability calculation.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate logging of system uptime and downtime.
Correct calculation of availability percentage.
